text: Right now there's a zombie pressed up against my gate, and it's wearing my best friend's uniform.
pic: Through the bars: dead Marcus pressed against the sporting goods gate.

text: Behind him, the hallway is full of them.
pic: The hallway behind him, full of them.

text: The radio on his chest is about to tell every one of them exactly where I'm hiding.
pic: Close on the radio clipped to his chest, circled. Danny on the floor, hand over his mouth.

text: An hour ago, I was basically the king of this mall.
pic: Danny in Lily's paper crown holding up his keys. Rewind. Then the title card: CHAPTER ONE, THE KING OF THE MALL.

text: Let me back up.
pic: Danny in Lily's paper crown holding up his keys. Rewind. Then the title card: CHAPTER ONE, THE KING OF THE MALL.

text: I have a key to every store in this mall.
pic: Danny holds up the key ring in the concourse.

text: The man who gave them to me said never to use the last one.
pic: Close on the ring: one key with a red tag.

text: I'm Danny. I do night security at Maplecrest Mall, and yeah, I've heard every mall cop joke there is.
pic: Danny in the concourse. Name tag: DANNY RUIZ, NIGHT GUARD.

text: I work nights so I can be at the bus stop at three-fifteen when my daughter Lily gets off.
pic: The bus stop, the 3:15 clock, Lily running off the bus.

text: My shift is nine to five. Mostly I walk, I check doors, and I eat the pretzels the food court guy was going to throw out anyway.
pic: Danny on his rounds with a pretzel, checking a door.

text: She's seven, and she thinks I'm the king of the mall. She drew me a picture once, me in a crown, holding up my keys. It's taped to the monitor in the security office.
pic: Lily's crayon drawing, MY DAD IS THE KING OF THE MALL, taped to a monitor.

text: We live with my mom, on the tenth floor of the Parkview Apartments, right across the highway.
pic: Night: Parkview tower across the highway. Tenth floor, fourth window, circled.

text: Every night at nine, when I walk in to work, Lily blinks her lamp at the mall three times.
pic: The window blinks: one, two, three. 9:00 PM.

text: It means I love you. I blink my flashlight back.
pic: Danny in the parking lot answers with three flashes.

text: I taught her one more signal, S-O-S, for emergencies. She thinks it's a game.
pic: The window blinks SOS.

text: I really hope she never has to use it.
pic: Danny looks up at the lit window.

text: Forty-two keys. Old Walt had this job before me, and when he handed them over, he tapped the last one.
pic: The security office: old Walt hands Danny the ring.

text: "That one, you never use," he said. "Don't ask."
pic: Close on Walt, serious.

text: Its tag says B3. There is no B3 on the mall map.
pic: The tag reads B3. The mall map, with no B3 anywhere.

text: Tonight, I'd only need one of them.
pic: The padlock on the sporting goods gate.

text: In thirty days, I'd find out what the last one opens.
pic: A steel door in the dark, stencilled B3.

text: Every night at one a.m., my best friend tells me a terrible joke on the radio.
pic: Danny in the security office, radio in hand. 1:00 AM.

text: Tonight, he whispered.
pic: Close on the radio.

text: Marcus guards the parking garage. He's twenty-two, he's studying to be a nurse, and he still owes me twenty bucks.
pic: Marcus in the garage with his nursing book. MARCUS, 22, NURSING STUDENT, OWES ME $20.

text: He lost a bet on a football game back in September, and he's been dodging me ever since.
pic: Marcus grinning, turning out empty pockets.

text: At one on the dot, the radio clicks.
pic: The radio on the desk crackles.

text: Danny. Why don't zombies ever eat clowns?
pic: Marcus grinning into his radio, then laughing at his own joke.

text: Because they taste funny.
pic: Marcus grinning into his radio, then laughing at his own joke.

text: He laughs at his own jokes. Every single time.
pic: Danny, half a smile.

text: At one-forty, the radio clicks again.
Danny. There's a guy on the ramp. He's walking... wrong.
pic: Marcus crouched by a car. A man limping up the ramp.

text: Marcus doesn't whisper. Ever.
pic: Close on Danny's face.

text: Sir? Sir, are you okay? You're bleeding...
pic: Marcus stepping toward the man.

text: Then the radio did something I'd never heard it do.
pic: Danny stares at the radio.

text: It went completely silent.
pic: The waves stop. NO SIGNAL.

text: I said his name into the radio. Then I said it again. Nothing.
pic: Danny with the radio to his mouth.

text: The security office has a wall of screens, one for every camera in the building.
pic: The office: the wall of monitors glowing.

text: In six years, the most exciting thing I've seen on them is a raccoon in the food court. Twice. Same raccoon.
pic: A security-camera shot of the food court with a raccoon on a table. Then the same raccoon again.

text: I pulled up camera six. The garage, level two.
pic: Security camera: garage, level two. CAM 6.

text: Marcus was on the ground, and the man from the ramp was on top of him.
pic: Security camera: Marcus down, the man over him.

text: Behind them, more were coming up the ramp from the highway. Six. Ten. Thirty.
pic: Security camera: the ramp filling up. Counter: 6, 10, 30.

text: They weren't running. They just walked, all at the same slow speed, like a crowd leaving a stadium.
pic: The crowd on the ramp, all walking the same way.

text: Danny... don't come down. Lock up.
pic: Security camera: Marcus on the ground, his hand on his radio.

text: I'd like to tell you I ran down there. I didn't. I stood in that office with my hand on the door, and I watched.
pic: Danny frozen at the office door, hand on the handle, the screens glowing behind him.

text: Then I picked up the phone and called nine-one-one. It rang and rang, and then a recording said all circuits were busy.
pic: Danny with the desk phone. ALL CIRCUITS ARE BUSY.

text: My mom's phone went straight to voicemail. So did the next nine calls.
pic: Danny's phone: MOM, calling. Voicemail. A call log, ten times.

text: And then every one of them on that screen turned the same way. Not toward the street. Toward the mall.
pic: Security camera: the whole crowd turns toward the mall.

text: One camera after another, I watched them come inside. The loading dock. The service hall. The doors by the restrooms.
pic: The monitor wall, screen after screen showing them coming in.

text: The only screen that stayed black was camera fourteen, the hallway behind the food court. It had been out since Tuesday. I'd put in a ticket.
pic: One black monitor: CAM 14, NO SIGNAL. A sticky note: TICKET PUT IN TUESDAY.

text: They were all heading for the food court. And the food court is made of glass.
pic: The food court's glass wall, and the crowd massing outside it.

text: I did the math. At the speed they were walking, I had about four minutes.
pic: A countdown: 4:00.

text: Four minutes to pick the one store I'd survive in. Which one would you pick?
pic: The mall map with four stores marked, and a question mark.

text: Here's the thing about malls. They're built to let people in. That's the whole point of them.
pic: The wide concourse, entrances everywhere.

text: But every store has a steel gate. And I have every key.
pic: Store gates; the key ring.

text: The pharmacy has medicine. It's also all glass.
pic: The pharmacy: all glass front. A red X.

text: The food court has food, and that's exactly where they're going.
pic: The food court, the crowd heading for it. A red X.

text: The department store has beds, and nine different entrances.
pic: The department store, nine arrows. A red X.

text: And Summit Outdoors has tents, water filters, baseball bats, and one way in.
pic: Summit Outdoors: tents, bats, one gate. A green check.

text: Every night guard has a zombie plan. Mine was Summit Outdoors. I just never thought I'd actually use it.
pic: Danny's old doodle of the plan on a napkin: SUMMIT OUTDOORS, circled.

text: Mall cops aren't exactly famous for running. I ran.
pic: Danny running down the concourse.

text: Down the escalator, past the fountain, past the pretzel place, with the keys already in my hand.
pic: Running past the escalator and the fountain, speed lines.

text: I was ten feet from the gate when I heard it.
pic: Danny at the Summit Outdoors front, freezing.

text: Behind me, the food court doors exploded.
pic: The food court glass bursts inward.

text: Key thirty-one. Under the gate, pull it down, lock it.
pic: The gate coming down; the padlock; tag 31.

text: I've done that a thousand times. I have never done it that fast.
pic: Danny's hands on the lock.

text: Then I sat down in the dark, between the tents, with my hand over my mouth.
pic: Danny sitting between the tents, hand over his mouth.

text: Through the gate, I could hear them filling up the hallway. Shuffling. Bumping into things. Dozens of feet that never quite left the floor.
pic: Shapes passing beyond the gate.

text: I did the breathing thing Lily learned in second grade. In for four. Out for four.
pic: Danny breathing slowly; a little memory of Lily showing him.

text: Once, something leaned on my gate, and the whole thing groaned. Then it moved on.
pic: The gate bulges inward, then settles.

text: Lily's drawing was still up in the security office. I remember thinking, the king of the mall is hiding in a tent.
pic: The crayon drawing; then Danny peeking out of a tent.

text: Twenty minutes went by. Then thirty.
pic: Clock: 2:08. Then 2:18.

text: I started to think maybe that was it. They'd wander off, and in the morning it'd be on the news, and I'd be a funny story.
pic: Danny's head back against a tent pole, almost smiling.

text: And then somebody knocked.
pic: The dark gate.

text: One knock. Two quick ones. One more.
pic: Knuckles on the gate.

text: Our knock. The one Marcus and I use on the office door.
pic: Danny's eyes, wide.

text: Danny. It's me.
pic: A shape at the gate.

text: He knew which store I'd pick. Of course he did.
pic: Danny, closing his eyes.

text: I turned on my flashlight for one second.
pic: Click: the flashlight beam.

text: His face was gray. And his whole sleeve was dark and wet.
pic: Marcus behind the bars, gray, his sleeve dark.

text: I had the key in my hand.
pic: Close on the key in Danny's hand.

text: Come on, man. Open it. Please.
pic: Marcus at the gate, hand on the bars.

text: There was a bite on his arm. I could see it in the light.
pic: His arm, a dark mark on it.

text: And past him, at the end of the hall, there were dozens of them. Standing still. Listening.
pic: The far end of the hallway: a crowd standing still.

text: If I opened that gate, they'd all come in with him.
pic: The lock, the key, the crowd beyond.

text: My hand was shaking so hard the keys were rattling. I had to press them against my chest to make them stop.
pic: Shaking keys, pressed to his chest.

text: Marcus watched my face. And he got it before I did.
pic: Marcus's face, understanding.

text: Hey. It's okay. I wouldn't open it either.
pic: Marcus, a tired smile.

text: He sat down with his back against the bars, and I sat down on my side, and we whispered for forty minutes.
pic: The two of them back to back, the gate between them.

text: About stupid stuff. The Bills. His mom's lasagna. The time he got locked in a fitting room at the department store and I had to come get him out.
pic: Warm memory pictures: a football game, a lasagna, Marcus in a fitting room.

text: I'm not gonna lie, man. I'm kind of scared.
pic: Marcus, head back against the bars.

text: So was I. I told him I was right here, and I wasn't going anywhere. Which was true. That was the whole problem.
pic: Danny's hand flat against the gate.

text: Tell Lily the king's still in his castle.
pic: Marcus, eyes closed.

text: Then, because he's Marcus, he told me one more terrible joke.
pic: Marcus grins.

text: What's a zombie's favorite kind of bean?
pic: Marcus, grinning.

text: A human bean.
pic: Marcus laughing weakly.

text: It wasn't funny. I laughed so hard I had to put my face in a sleeping bag.
pic: Danny with his face in a sleeping bag, shoulders shaking.

text: And Danny? I still owe you twenty bucks.
pic: Marcus's hand on the bars.

text: At two thirty-one, Marcus stopped breathing.
pic: Clock: 2:31 AM. Marcus still.

text: At two thirty-nine, he stood up.
pic: Clock: 2:39 AM. Marcus rising.

text: He didn't look at me. He just stood there with his face against the bars.
pic: Dead Marcus at the gate.

text: Two forty-five in the morning. That's where you came in.
pic: The cold-open picture again. 2:45 AM.

text: Then my radio crackled.
pic: Danny's radio on the floor, its light on.

text: Is anyone still in the mall? I'm on the second floor of the department store. Please. I'm not alone up here.
pic: A radio wave icon. The department store, dark, second floor.

text: A woman. Whispering. Somewhere upstairs in my mall.
pic: The dark department store upstairs.

text: Her voice came out of my radio. And then, one second later, out of the radio on Marcus's chest.
pic: Both radios, one after the other.

text: Every head in that hallway turned.
pic: Every head turns.

text: Forty of them. One gate.
pic: The crowd and the one gate.

text: They didn't run at it. They leaned on it, all at once, the way a crowd leans on the doors on Black Friday.
pic: The crowd pressing on the gate; a flash of Black Friday shoppers at the doors.

text: And the steel started to bend.
pic: The gate bending.

text: And she was about to call again.
pic: The radio on Marcus's chest, its light on.

text: I switched my radio off. But his was still on.
pic: Click. Danny's radio dark. Marcus's still lit.

text: There was only one way to shut it up. I had to reach through the bars and take it off his chest.
pic: Danny's hand reaching through the bars.

text: His teeth were about an inch from my wrist. The whole time, he was looking right at me.
pic: Close: the hand, the radio, Marcus's face.

text: And the clip stuck. He always wore it upside down. I must have told him a hundred times.
pic: The clip, upside down.

text: I twisted it, and it came loose, and I fell back on the floor with it.
pic: Danny falling back with the radio.

text: I stuffed it as deep into a sleeping bag as it would go, and I lay there, not breathing.
pic: The radio pushed into a sleeping bag.

text: Without the noise, they forgot about me. It took maybe ten minutes. One by one, they drifted back down the hall.
pic: The crowd drifting away.

text: All except Marcus.
pic: Marcus alone at the gate.

text: Then, from inside the sleeping bag, she said my name.
pic: The sleeping bag. A faint glow inside.

text: When I grabbed that radio, I must have squeezed the talk button.
pic: The radio's talk button.

text: Danny, right? The night guard. I can hear you breathing.
pic: Radio waves.

text: She didn't sound scared anymore. She sounded like someone ordering a coffee.
pic: Danny staring at the radio.

text: Don't worry. I'm not one of them.
pic: Radio waves.

text: You've got all the keys, don't you?
pic: The key ring on Danny's belt.

text: I didn't say a word.
pic: Danny's hand over the radio.

text: That's okay. Get some sleep, Danny. We'll talk tomorrow.
pic: Radio waves.

text: Then the little light on the radio went out.
pic: The radio's light goes out.

text: I didn't sleep. I lay there and listened to Marcus lean on the gate every few minutes, like he was checking that it was still locked.
pic: Danny awake between the tents; Marcus leaning on the gate.

text: Here's what bothered me.
pic: The mall map.

text: The mall closes at nine. At midnight, I walked every hallway and checked every door, like I do every night. The department store was locked. I locked it.
pic: Danny on his midnight rounds, rattling the department store gate.

text: Nobody was in here.
pic: The empty mall at midnight.

text: So who was she? And what was she doing in my mall at two in the morning?
pic: The department store, dark, a light moving on the second floor.

text: I don't remember falling asleep. I remember waking up.
pic: Danny waking between the tents.

text: Gray light was coming down through the skylights, and the mall was quiet. Really quiet.
pic: Morning light in the concourse.

text: I waited an hour before I moved at all. Then I crawled to the gate, an inch at a time, to look.
pic: Danny crawling to the gate.

text: Out in the hallway, the dead were just standing there. Like they were waiting for the stores to open.
pic: The dead standing still in the morning concourse.

text: In the daylight, it all looked fake. Like a movie set somebody forgot to take down.
pic: The morning concourse, wide and still.

text: Then, way off down the hall, I heard a gate rattle.
pic: Far down the hall.

text: Then another one. Closer.
pic: Closer.

text: It was Marcus. He was walking the loop, shaking every gate he passed, the way he did every single night.
pic: Dead Marcus walking the loop, rattling gates.

text: He shook mine too. He didn't even look in.
pic: Marcus rattles Danny's gate and walks on.

text: Down by the escalator, the night cleaner from the food court was still pushing her cart into the same wall. Over and over.
pic: A dead cleaner pushing her cart into a wall.

text: That's when I figured out the first rule. They follow sound. And when it's quiet, they go back to whatever they used to do.
pic: RULE 1: THEY FOLLOW SOUND.

text: I had breakfast. A protein bar that tasted like a yoga mat.
pic: Danny chewing a protein bar.

text: Summit Outdoors by daylight: tents, kayaks, a whole wall of camping food, and a cardboard bear that scared me twice.
pic: The store by daylight; a cardboard bear cutout.

text: Then my phone buzzed. One message, sent at two-fourteen a.m.
pic: Danny's phone lights up: 1 NEW MESSAGE, 2:14 AM.

text: It was from my mom.
pic: The phone: MOM.

text: Lily is with me. Door locked. Do not come. And she typed the word not in all capitals.
pic: The text: LILY IS WITH ME. DOOR LOCKED. DO NOT COME.

text: My mom is seventy, and she's the toughest person I've ever met.
pic: Lita, Danny's mom, arms folded.

text: I texted back. Stay put. I love you. Tell Lily the king's still in his castle.
pic: Danny typing the reply.

text: It said delivered. Then the bars on my phone went to zero, and they never came back.
pic: DELIVERED. The signal bars drop to nothing.

text: There's a camping radio in the store, the kind with a hand crank. I found the emergency channel.
pic: Danny cranking a camping radio.

text: This is an emergency broadcast. Shelter in place. Rescue teams will reach every area within thirty days.
pic: EMERGENCY BROADCAST: SHELTER IN PLACE. RESCUE WITHIN 30 DAYS.

text: It played the same thirty seconds, over and over, all day.
pic: The camping radio, its dial glowing.

text: Thirty days. Okay. I can do thirty days. I've done diets longer than that.
pic: DAY 1 OF 30.

text: So I counted what I had.
pic: The store's shelves.

text: Seventy-two bottles of water. Forty protein bars. A shelf of freeze-dried meals, a camp stove, water filters, and more baseball bats than anybody needs.
pic: Supplies counted up on screen.

text: If I'm careful, that's water for about twelve days.
pic: WATER: 12 DAYS.

text: Then I remembered something, and my stomach dropped.
pic: Danny goes still.

text: My mom is diabetic. Her insulin lasts about ten days.
pic: An insulin pen. INSULIN: 10 DAYS.

text: Rescue was thirty days away. My mom's insulin would run out in ten.
pic: Two countdowns: 30 and 10.

text: There's a ladder in the stockroom that goes up to a hatch on the roof.
pic: The stockroom ladder and the hatch.

text: Six years I've worked here, and I'd never once been up there.
pic: Danny climbing out onto the roof.

text: From the roof, you can see the whole highway.
pic: The highway from the roof.

text: The sun was out. That felt kind of rude.
pic: Blue sky over the highway.

text: Eight lanes of cars, all stopped, doors hanging open. And the dead, walking between them like they'd forgotten where they parked.
pic: Stopped cars, open doors, the dead walking between them.

text: Smoke over downtown. A helicopter that flew right over me and didn't stop.
pic: Smoke on the skyline; a helicopter passing over.

text: I waved at it like an idiot. Both arms.
pic: Danny waving both arms at the sky.

text: On the roof of the hotel next door, somebody had painted help on a bedsheet. Nobody came for them either.
pic: A bedsheet on a roof: HELP.

text: And on the other side of all of it, a mile and a half away, Parkview. Tenth floor, fourth window from the left.
pic: Parkview tower in the distance; the window circled.

text: I could see my daughter's window from the roof of this mall. It might as well have been the moon.
pic: Danny small on the roof; the tower far away.

text: I know what you're thinking. Just go.
pic: Danny looking at the highway.

text: My car is in the garage, with them. There are eight lanes of the dead between me and that building.
pic: The garage; the highway full of the dead.

text: And if I somehow made it, I'd be leading every one of them straight to her door.
pic: A line of the dead following one figure to the tower's door.

text: So I stayed up there, and I watched her window all afternoon. I counted every window on that building twice.
pic: The sun moving down; Danny watching.

text: At eight fifty-nine, the whole city went dark. Including her window.
pic: 8:59 PM. The city goes black.

text: No streetlights. No windows. I could barely see the shape of her building against the sky.
pic: The black city; the tower's outline against the sky.

text: At nine, I turned on my flashlight and pointed it at her building, just in case.
pic: Danny on the dark roof, flashlight pointed at the tower.

text: Nine o'clock. Nothing.
pic: 9:00 PM. Nothing.

text: Nine-oh-one. Nothing.
pic: 9:01 PM. Nothing.

text: I stood there with my flashlight, telling myself the power's out, she can't, it's fine.
pic: Danny on the roof with his flashlight.

text: Then, one. Two. Three.
pic: A light in the window: one, two, three.

text: Not her lamp. A flashlight. In the tenth-floor window.
pic: The tenth-floor window.

text: She's alive. She figured it out. She's seven years old, and she figured it out.
pic: Danny's face.

text: I blinked back three times. Then I sat down on the roof, and I couldn't stop shaking.
pic: Danny blinks back three times, then sits down.

text: Then the radio in my pocket clicked on. Marcus's radio. I'd carried it around all day.
pic: Marcus's radio in Danny's pocket, its light on.

text: That's sweet, Danny.
pic: Radio waves.

text: She'd been watching.
pic: Danny, very still.

text: Who's in the window?
pic: The tower window, tiny, far away.
